chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from al-Hasan al-Qummi, from Idris ibn Abdullah, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the interpretation of this verse:
What has brought you into Saqar? They will say: We were not of the musallin.
He عليه السلام said: What is meant by it is: We were not among the followers of the Imams, those concerning whom Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said:
And the foremost are the foremost; those are the ones brought near.

Do you not see that people call the one who comes after the foremost in the race a musalli? So that is what was meant where He said, We were not of the musallin, meaning: we were not among the followers of the foremost.

key_terms.السَّابِقُونَ: the foremost ones, understood here as the leading divinely chosen figures
key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةِ: the Imams who are to be followed
key_terms.الْمُصَلِّينَ: those who follow the foremost ones, according to this interpretation
key_terms.تَفْسِيرِ: interpretation or explanation of the verse
key_terms.سَقَرَ: Saqar, a name of Hellfire in the verse

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام interpret 'We were not of the musallin' in Surah al-Muddaththir?
ai.summary: This hadith interprets the verse about the people of Saqar by explaining that al-musallin here refers to those who follow the foremost ones, identified as the Imams عليه السلام. It draws on the linguistic usage of musalli as one who comes directly after the leader in a race, linking the verse to wilayah and following the divinely appointed leaders. The narration therefore presents the verse as a Qur'anic allusion to religious authority and salvation.
